texts: If the ASD is restrictive, the Qp:Qs will rarely exceed 2:1: B.
The size of an ASD shunt depends on the size of the defect and on the relative compliance of the two ventricles; once the hole is small enough to restrict flow, the shunt stays modest.
The location of the defect has little influence on the shunt, while mitral stenosis increases it (Lutembacher syndrome).
Heart failure in an infant is seldom caused by an isolated ASD, and the onset of pulmonary hypertension is not predictable.
In the picture, only a thin stream passes the small hole, and the money bucket never passes twice the orca bucket.
Memory hook: a narrow hole: the money bucket rarely passes twice the orca's.
